description:
`check_function_clauses` (src/compiler2/source_diagnostics.rs:41) is purely
SYNTACTIC. It builds `PatternRow::<Ty>` rows with `preconditions: Vec::new()` and
`guard: None`, and bails entirely on guards and externs:

    if surface.extern_abi.is_some()
        || surface.clauses.iter().any(|clause| clause.guard.is_some()) {
        return;
    }

So it warns from clause SHAPE alone, with no knowledge of which inputs a function
can actually receive.

## Measured consequence

44 `warning[type/no-matching-clause]` occurrences across 19
`fixtures2/behavior/*.diagnostics` files. 25 of the 44 point at RUNTIME LIBRARY
sources -- runtime:Enum.fz 21, runtime:List.fz 2, runtime:Range.fz 1,
runtime:Map.fz 1 -- i.e. library functions warn once per USE SITE, in fixtures
that never call the un-matched shape.

`fixtures2/behavior/quicksort.expected.diagnostics` still carries exactly the two
warnings the old ticket names, on `fn append([h | t], ys)` and
`fn qsort([p | rest])`.

## The proposed mechanism is available

`ActivationInputAlternatives` exists (semantic.rs:766) and
`calculate_dispatch_reachability` still computes `fail_reachable` per row
(dispatch_reachability.rs:22, field at :15). Moving the lint after type inference
and warning only when the failure row is genuinely reachable is buildable today.

## Why this is a judgment call, not a bug

It is a decision about where a lint lives and what gets re-blessed. Moving it
changes 44 golden lines across 19 files, and it trades a conservative
always-warn for a precision-dependent warn -- which is only as good as the
reachability analysis under it.

## What the old ticket got wrong

The two runtime library functions it names, `map_list` and `with_index_list`, NO
LONGER EXIST (`grep -rn "fn map_list\|fn with_index_list"
src/modules/runtime_library/*.fz` -> 0 hits). The CLASS it points at is intact;
substitute runtime:Enum.fz, which carries 21 of the 44 blessed warnings.

Its stated blockers are fz-f98.11 (now fz-kdt.14) and fz-f98.9 (now fz-kdt.36).

## Checks

- A library function warns only where its un-matched shape is actually reachable;
  quicksort's two warnings either survive with a reachability justification or
  disappear.
- The 44 blessed warnings across 19 diagnostics files are re-derived, and the
  diff is explained per file rather than blanket-blessed.
title: Move the no-matching-clause lint after type inference so it warns only on a reachable failure row
